title: Staggered window thresholds and KV-revival heuristic for continuous batcher
author: Priya Singh
description: Context: Continuous-batching latency spikes remain correlated with long-lived, low-KV-hit requests that accumulate in a single queue window and prevent small fast requests from being coalesced. Motivation: previous fixes (deadline steering, probe jitter) reduced some tail pain but left scenarios where a small number of KV-heavy requests would create a persistent backlog and cause cascading micro-timeouts in downstream queues. This PR introduces two coordinated strategies: 1) staggered window thresholds (per-priority, per-queue moving thresholds) that allow the batcher to open secondary ingestion windows when primary windows are clogged; 2) a lightweight KV-revival heuristic that performs a fast, opportunistic KV pre-warm for requests that are likely to unblock the cache and restore batching efficiency. The changes are safe-by-default, revertible, and covered by unit + perf tests.
commits: 5 commits: (1) add staggered window scheduling skeleton; (2) implement per-priority moving thresholds; (3) KV-revival probe and metrics; (4) tests + docs; (5) canary rollout config
review_comments: Ethan Moore: Questioned CPU impact of KV-revival during high throughput; asked for upper bound throttle and accounting in metrics.
Priya Singh: Added a token-bucket throttle (configurable) and instrumentation (kv_revive_attempts, kv_revive_success). Updated PR with throttle default=2 revives/sec per worker.
Sofia Chen: Requested clearer invariants for window promotion to avoid oscillation under bursty arrival patterns.
Priya Singh: Introduced hysteresis (min_promotion_interval=100ms) and a backoff multiplier. Added tests that simulate bursty arrivals to assert no oscillation observed.
Miguel Alvarez: Confirmed no change to public API and asked for rollout plan and rollback safety nets.
Priya Singh: Added canary.yaml to repo and rollout_plan section in PR description; tested rollback path (feature flag + immediate disable) in perf-lab.
Sofia Chen: Approved after seeing perf numbers and tests. Ethan Moore: Approved. Miguel Alvarez: Merged after canary verification.
bench_summary: Perf lab (mixed small/large request mix): median latency improved 5.8% overall; p99 reduced ~22% for prioritized small requests on congested queues; throughput increased ~8% under sustained mixed load. KV-hit-rate improved by ~6 percentage points in scenarios where revival successfully warmed frequently-missed keys. Observed CV of batch sizes decreased indicating more consistent batching behavior.
rollout_plan: Phased canary: 2% traffic for 6 hours, observe metrics (batch_window_utilization, queue_escape_count, p99); if stable, ramp to 10% for 12 hours, then full rollout. Immediate rollback by disabling feature flag or reverting canary service routing. Ops runbook added in docs link.
observability_changes: metrics added: batch_window_utilization, window_promotion_count, kv_revive_attempts, kv_revive_success, queue_escape_count
release_notes: Staggered window thresholds for the continuous batcher and a best-effort KV-revival probe. Improves tail latency for mixed workloads and reduces starvation risk when KV-heavy requests appear. Configurable via feature flag and runtime params.
notes_for_ops: Default config is conservative: promotion hysteresis 100ms, max 2 kv-revives/sec per worker, revival cost capped by token bucket. If ops see CPU spike correlated with kv_revive_attempts, set 'kv_revival.enabled=false' and reroute canary until investigation completes.
additional_context: Related to ENG-5481 (scheduler stability under asymmetric KV loads). Complements previous deadline-steering and probe-jitter PRs but targets long-lived backlog patterns by allowing controlled secondary windows and active cache nudges.
author_acknowledgement: Author confirms feature-flag gating and that all new metrics are backward-compatible. No user-facing API changes.
